question: Which gas is evolved during the burning of natural gas (CH₄)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**CO₂.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Natural gas** is primarily composed of **methane (CH₄)**, which is a** hydrocarbon.**
 
• When natural gas is burned in the **presence of oxygen**, it undergoes **combustion, **which results in the release of energy and the formation of new compounds.
 
• One of the main products of the combustion of natural gas is **carbon dioxide (CO₂)**, which is a** greenhouse gas** that contributes to global warming.
 
• Other products of the combustion of natural gas can include **water vapor (H₂O) and nitrogen oxides (NOₓ)**, which can contribute to air pollution and have negative health effects.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **NH₃** is **ammonia**, which can be produced by other processes, such as the** Haber-Bosch process** for synthesizing fertilizer.
 
• **N₂** is nitrogen gas, which is an **inert gas** that does not typically react during combustion.
 
 
• However, some **nitrogen oxides (**NOx) can be produced as byproducts of combustion.
 
 
 
• **H₂ **is hydrogen gas, which can be produced by the **decomposition of methane **under certain conditions.
 
• Hydrogen gas is also a** potential fuel source** that is being explored as an **alternative to fossil fuels.**
